$comment: THE STARTER PACK, AS DATA. Phase 5 of install.md presents these entries and declares what the
user approves; this file is the same set with the arguments that prose could not be tested for.
WHY IT EXISTS. The pack's rule half was broken three independent ways and every one was found by
review rather than by a test: `scope` defaulted to agent and the declaration was refused outright,
breadth confined every entry to the install circle, and `memory_ratify` throws on a rule id. All
three lived in the prose saying HOW to declare, so a test that parsed the entry list and chose the
arguments itself would have passed however wrong the playbook was.
THE PROSE STAYS AUTHORITATIVE FOR A HUMAN; this is authoritative for the machine, and
starter-pack.test.ts fails if the two disagree in either direction.

entries.content: Make the smallest change that meets the request; improvements outside it are proposals, not edits.
entries.reason: unrequested changes cost more to review than they save

entries.content: Batch questions: collect what needs asking and ask once.
entries.reason: drip-fed questions interrupt more than they resolve

entries.content: A claim of done carries the evidence that proves it: the command, the output, the diff.
Name the cause before shipping the fix.
If a secret, key, or token is about to enter a file or commit, stop and say so.
Seed a new circle's baseline in one batch of grouped questions rather than one correction at a time, and store only what the user's standing files do not already cover.
entries.reason: an unseeded circle costs the user months of re-explaining the same norms on every new project
